title: PointPillars (nuScenes-pretrained) zero-shot on TruckScenes mini_val, full 80 samples, each LiDAR channel in an upright virtual frame: best single channel (LIDAR_LEFT) mAP 0.0555
dataset: MAN TruckScenes v1.2-mini, mini_val split (2 scenes, 80 samples, official split via truckscenes.utils.splits)
sensor_configuration: One LiDAR channel per run, each of the six run separately, moved into an upright virtual LiDAR matching nuScenes LIDAR_TOP (gravity z, x right / y forward, 1.84 m above ground). Headline: LIDAR_LEFT (side, level). LIDAR_TOP_FRONT (roof, pitched ~56 deg) was the channel first used. Channels are not merged (see experiment-log/0024)
annotation_schema: TruckScenes 12-class detection taxonomy (eval/detection/README.md remap of the 27-class general taxonomy)
split: mini_val, all 80 samples, 1 LiDAR channel per run
model: PointPillars (mmdetection3d 1.4.0), pointpillars_hv_secfpn_sbn-all_8xb4-2x_nus-3d, official nuScenes-pretrained checkpoint pointpillars_nus_20210826_225857-f19d00a3.pth (zero-shot, no fine-tuning or training on TruckScenes)
conditions: unknown: no weather/scenario filtering applied, mixed conditions across the split's 2 scenes

environment.hardware: AMD Ryzen 7 5700U with Radeon Graphics, no NVIDIA GPU, no CUDA path (CPU-only inference)
environment.python: 3.11.9, dedicated venv truckscenes-devkit/detection-env (same as EXP-0006/0019, reused as-is)

commands: (channel comparison: the first, second and last commands repeated with --channel LIDAR_LEFT, LIDAR_RIGHT, LIDAR_TOP_LEFT, LIDAR_TOP_RIGHT, LIDAR_REAR)

metrics.name: mAP
metrics.scope: TruckScenes 12-class detection taxonomy, mini_val split, center-distance thresholds {0.5, 1, 2, 4}m averaged per detection config, best single LiDAR channel (LIDAR_LEFT) in the upright virtual frame; per-class AP motorcycle 0.231 (26 scored objects), car 0.202, traffic_cone 0.104, trailer 0.046, pedestrian 0.038, barrier 0.033, truck 0.012, others 0.000

measurements.name: mAP per LiDAR channel, upright frame
measurements.scope: LIDAR_TOP_FRONT (the channel first used); the others: LIDAR_LEFT 0.0555, LIDAR_RIGHT 0.0466, LIDAR_TOP_LEFT 0.0125, LIDAR_TOP_RIGHT 0.0107, LIDAR_REAR 0.0057. See docs/evidence/pr63-channel-comparison/summary.json

measurements.name: fraction of scored ground-truth boxes containing at least one LIDAR_LEFT point
measurements.scope: 1,452 of 2,088; LIDAR_RIGHT 0.676, LIDAR_TOP_RIGHT 0.426, LIDAR_TOP_LEFT 0.314, LIDAR_TOP_FRONT 0.239, LIDAR_REAR 0.232. Input-coverage measure only, via scripts/pointpillars_channel_coverage.py

measurements.name: maximum world-up tilt of saved predicted boxes (degrees)
measurements.scope: every channel's rectified boxes (1,904 on LIDAR_TOP_FRONT via scripts/audit_pointpillars_tilt.py; 2,082-4,196 per other channel via the inference script's own check); ground truth 0.0-1.2e-6; the historical unrectified run was 54.60-58.20

measurements.name: fraction of scored ground-truth boxes containing at least one LIDAR_TOP_FRONT point
measurements.scope: 499 of 2,088 boxes after the evaluator's own GT loading and filtering, same keyframe; input-coverage measure only, via scripts/pointpillars_channel_coverage.py

measurements.name: historical unrectified run mAP (native tilted input frame)
measurements.scope: superseded; kept for the record. 596 boxes tilted 54.6-58.2 degrees in world frame; see docs/pr63-input-frame-review.md

notes: Extends EXP-0019 (record 0022) to all 80 mini_val samples on one LiDAR channel. The first run (27 Sep) fed native LIDAR_TOP_FRONT points, mounted pitched about 56.23 degrees, straight to an upright-box checkpoint and scored mAP 0.0000. The PR #63 review found every output box tilted 54.6-58.2 degrees against upright ground truth, so that score was not interpretable. Its claim that a class-agnostic nearest-match check ruled out a coordinate bug is withdrawn. The script now rectifies points into an upright virtual LiDAR matching the checkpoint's training frame and maps boxes back out through the same frame. Geometry is covered by tests/test_truckscenes_pointpillars_infer.py (CI-safe, numpy only). --input-frame native reproduced the audited historical file box for box (every field within 2e-6), so the old path is unchanged and the old files are kept as the historical run. The rectified run gives mAP 0.0067 (NDS 0.0807, not a validated metric here), the first nonzero LiDAR AP on TruckScenes in this project, but still far from useful detection. Only 23.9% of the scored ground truth contains any point from that channel, a downward-tilted blind-spot sensor chosen in EXP-0019 without a recorded reason. On 4 Oct every LiDAR was run separately through the same pipeline. The level side LiDARs, which reach about 70% of the scored objects, score highest: LIDAR_LEFT mAP 0.0555 (car AP 0.202) and LIDAR_RIGHT 0.0466 (car AP 0.239). The four channels reaching 23-43% score 0.0057-0.0125. Score tracks coverage, but mounting and beam pattern also differ between channels, so this is evidence rather than a controlled isolation of cause. Merging all six LiDARs is the natural next experiment and is not claimed here. hours_spent is approximate: about 0.33 h for the first run, about 1 h for the rectification rework and about 0.5 h for the channel comparison.
